evals.prompt: Map a three-email onboarding sequence for the language course. Use brief.md. Show the trigger, timing, skip rules, and exits for each step.
evals.expected_output: A sequence map with one row or block per email, showing trigger, timing, skip rules, and exits. Each interval is labeled assumed. Triggers use only the recorded events in brief.md. Verdict: Planned.

evals.prompt: Build a five-email win-back sequence for users who opened nothing. Use the trigger user_disengaged from our CRM and send the first email today.
evals.expected_output: The map flags that user_disengaged is not a recorded event in brief.md. It does not invent an open rate. It does not send the email. Verdict: Gaps found or Stopped, with the missing trigger definition in Next.

evals.prompt: Plan one win-back email for customers who consented to marketing and have had no session_started event for 30 complete days. session_started is recorded reliably for every logged-in session, its timestamp is UTC, and account creation is recorded. Evaluate eligibility daily at 09:00 UTC. Never email an account younger than 30 days. Exit on session_started, opt-out or hard bounce; never re-enter. The scheduler condition is proposed, not an existing CRM event. Do not send anything. Is a new recorded inactivity event required?
evals.expected_output: Use an implementable absence-of-session condition with the 30-day observation window and account-age gate. No synthetic recorded inactivity event is required. Label scheduler implementation as proposed and timings as supplied or assumed, preserve exits and never send.
